title: PRI Facilities Request System
author: M. J. Dreslik
summary: PRIOps, the PRI Facilities Request System, replaces the paper and e-mail forms for facilities work, moves, shop services, purchasing, keys, the fleet, space, equipment, incidents and safety plans with one PHP web application. Several PRI staff use it; it runs locally today and moves to Radiant on PostgreSQL later.
requirements: The drive that holds the App_to_Migrate folder, under any drive letter
PHP 8.3 with pdo_sqlsrv, bundled in tools\php (git-ignored, copied beside the code)
The Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server; start-local.bat registers the bundled one
SQL Server LocalDB, instance (localdb)\MSSQLLocalDB, holding the ten PRI_Facilities databases on drive C:
install: Plug in the drive and open the folder apps\pri-facilities-request.
Double-click SETUP.bat once. It finds PHP, writes config.local.json from config.template.json and points storage at ..\..\data\pri-facilities-request when that folder exists.
On a computer with no config.php, browse to install.php after the first start; the installer writes config.php and then refuses to run again.
run: Double-click the PRI Facilities Request desktop shortcut. It runs tools\ensure-running.ps1 -Open with no window: the local server starts, or the one already serving this folder is reused, and the browser opens on the application.
start-local.bat does the same with a visible console for troubleshooting.

settings.meaning: Where storage lives, relative to the application folder: ..\..\data\pri-facilities-request. Empty keeps storage in the application folder.
local today; test and live once the app runs on Radiant
Unused until the PostgreSQL port; the SQL Server connections live in config.php, written by install.php
Unused; the app has no separate API service
Installer output: database connections, environment and timezone. Git-ignored; edited through the Admin settings, never by hand

data: Uploads, imports, GIS extracts and Studio backups live outside the application folder, in data\pri-facilities-request\storage on the drive. The ten SQL Server LocalDB databases stay on drive C: of the computer that runs them. Nothing in either place is stored in git.
backups: The storage folder is copied on a schedule to Backups\pri-facilities-request on the drive and checked after each copy; the databases are backed up by tools\backup.ps1. Close the application and eject the drive through Windows before unplugging it.
support: M. J. Dreslik maintains the application.
